definition: Natural Language Web or NLWeb was introduced by Microsoft in 2025.
details: It is an open Python project designed to simplify the creation of natural language interfaces for websites. It enables users to query website contents using natural language, similar to interacting with an AI assistant. Every instance functions as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server allowing websites to make their content discoverable and accessible to AI agents and other participants. NLWeb leverages existing web standards like Schema.org and RSS to build conversational capabilities of processing user queries through language models, performing semantic searches against website content and generating natural responses. It is platform-agnostic, running on all major systems and connecting to any vector database. Content to be indexed by NLWeb works best when it is organized in an AI friendly way. This means short, interlinked and semantically annotated articles work best. Initial adopters of NLWeb include TripAdvisor, Shopify, Eventbrite, and Hearst.

explainer.lead: NLWeb, or Natural Language Web, is an open Python project Microsoft introduced in 2025 to simplify building natural language interfaces for websites. It matters because it lets users query a site conversationally and makes site content discoverable to AI agents.

tiers.eli5: It lets a website answer questions typed in plain language, the way you'd ask an AI assistant.
tiers.practitioner: Developers use it so each instance acts as a Model Context Protocol server, exposing site content to AI agents and other participants. A pitfall is that visibility to agents depends on the site's content being structured with standards like Schema.org and RSS.
tiers.paperLevel: An open Python project in which every instance functions as an MCP server, leveraging Schema.org and RSS to build conversational querying of site content. No formal limits are stated.

explainer.example: A site built with NLWeb could answer a natural-language question about its contents and simultaneously expose that content to an AI agent through its MCP server.
